text:
ada: quick RFC follow-up: i'm prototyping a tiny decision DAG for choosing fp8/int8/4bit at request time. want quick eyes.
leo: DAG? curious how that's different from ruleset.
ada: DAG lets us express precedence & short-circuiting: e.g., if high_confidence_prompt -> use int4 fast path, else evaluate quality nodes. cheaper than scoring all lanes.
nina: makes sense. ensure nodes are cheap boolean checks mostly. avoid regex-heavy prompt scans in hot path.
chuck: we need per-tenant overrides and an emergency global-safe switch. can we param scope at runtime?
ada: yes: scope order: route-pin > tenant-override > org-default > global-default. each node gets evaluated with that scope resolution.
leo: storage model? immutable profiles with versioned ids? signed manifests?
ada: manifest stored in config-service with digital signature. runtime caches manifest + quick bloom check for hot routes. manifest includes node graph and lane order for tie-breaks.
nina: runtime behavior: decide once at request start. lock lane for entire request. allow sync-retry on failure with safer lane. no mid-stream swaps.
chuck: hysteresis and cooldowns?
ada: yes per (route,profile) cooldowns. also a minimal retry budget per minute set in manifest.
leo: telemetry: every decision emits quant_lane, manifest_id, node_path, decision_hash, calibration_age, mirror_tag. sample detailed decisions for 1% traffic.
nina: mirroring: run on safer lane in parallel for small fraction; compute BLEU/perplex deltas offline. keep mirror sample low for cost.
chuck: safety net: if reranker anomaly or llm-quality check fails, do immediate retry on safer lane for sync only and mark event. async jobs get retried via job-queue.
ada: calibration staleness rule baked in: if sample_count < min_samples or age>max_age we bias to safer lane. manifest exposes min_samples & max_age.
leo: deterministic tie-breaker: lane precedence list in manifest. if equal score pick earliest. document and test.
nina: interesting idea: add a small hardware hint node that reads gpu_temp/queue and votes for cheaper lane if overloaded. but keep it opt-in per-profile.
chuck: rollout semantics?
ada: draft: profile states: draft, canary, ramp, pinned. canary percent, max-error-rate, auto-pause threshold. also a rollback hook to pin global-safe-profile.
leo: config delivery: protobuf + signed crc over stream. runtime validates signature before applying.
ada: decision complexity: avoid per-token work. also provide a debug endpoint to re-evaluate a decision for a given request payload offline.
nina: ops-bot: scheduler: quant-decision-dag canary -> eng-ml-prod at 2026-03-25T04:00:00Z (PR#4599).
ada: i'll open PR with manifest schema, runtime shim, telemetry hooks, and canary playbook. comments welcome.
chuck: add an audit log for every canary decision (sampled) for postmortems.
ada: will do. tagging follow-up checklist in PR.
